title: Tata Sons Chief N Chandrasekaran earns Rs 685 crore compensation in 5 years
summary: Tata Sons executive chairman N Chandrasekaran received Rs 685 crore in compensation from Tata Trusts over the past five years, including Rs 158.6 crore in FY26. Most of his pay was commission and his FY26 package represented about 80% of total director remuneration at Tata Sons. The disclosure comes ahead of a mid‑August shareholder vote on his directorship.
content:
Tata Sons executive chairman N Chandrasekaran has received total compensation of Rs 685 crore from Tata Trusts over the last five years. In FY26, Chandrasekaran — widely referred to as Chandra — received total remuneration of Rs 158.6 crore from Tata Sons, the highest since FY22 when the company began disclosing remuneration details. According to data compiled by Moneycontrol, his pay last year stood at Rs 155 crore and in FY24 it was Rs 134.8 crore.

A large portion of the compensation paid to Chandra is in the form of commission. Of the Rs 158.6 crore he earned in FY26, Rs 140.7 crore was commission while Rs 17.9 crore was salary. The FY26 package amounted to about 80% of the total remuneration paid by Tata Sons to all of its directors combined.

For perspective, HCL’s CEO C Vijaykumar received Rs 176 crore in remuneration in FY26 and is regarded in various reports as one of the highest-paid executives in India. Persistent Systems CEO Sandeep Kalra received Rs 148 crore in FY25, which is lower than Chandra’s compensation. Hero MotoCorp’s Pawan Munjal was paid Rs 122 crore in FY26, the highest among auto company executives.

The disclosure of these figures comes as Chandra faces a crucial vote at the annual general meeting of Tata Sons in mid-August, where his directorship will be put to shareholders. Although his current five-year term as chairman runs until February 2027, he is required to retire by rotation and obtain majority shareholder approval to retain his director’s seat.

Saurabh Agrawal, the chief financial officer and executive director of Tata Sons, was the company’s second-highest-paid top manager, drawing a total income of Rs 34 crore in FY26, which included around Rs 26 crore as commission. Aside from Chandra and Agrawal, none of the other seven board members received regular remuneration. Six of those board members, however, received commissions in the range of Rs 1-3 crore. Venu Srinivasan, chairman emeritus of TVS Motors, was the only board member who received neither remuneration nor commission.

The figures underline the concentration of pay at the top of Tata Sons’ leadership and have drawn attention as shareholder approvals and governance questions come into focus at the upcoming AGM. The data and reporting originate from Moneycontrol and related company disclosures.
